author: John Baker
title: Harris' Plan After Declining California Governor Run - NewsBreak
text: Former Vice President Kamala Harris has announced she will not seek the governorship of California in the 2026 election, putting to rest widespread speculation of a potential run. Instead, Harris said she is focused on keeping her options open, and analysts now believe she is planning for a potential 2028 presidential run. Her decision clears the path for other Democrats to enter the race for governor, as many have withheld moving forward amid uncertainty regarding Harris’s plans. Harris acknowledged that a statewide campaign could restrict her options. She reaffirmed her commitment to supporting Democrats nationwide and pledged to share her future plans publicly. Harris stated, “I love this state, its people, and its promise. It is my home. But after deep reflection, I’ve decided that I will not run for Governor in this election.” Harris said, “For now, my leadership — and public service — will not be in elected office. I look forward to getting back out and listening to the American people, helping elect Democrats across the nation who will fight fearlessly, and sharing more details in the months ahead about my own plans.” With Harris withdrawing, prominent Democrats like former HHS Secretary Xavier Becerra and former Los Angeles Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa have emerged as key contenders. Harris previously served as California attorney general and U.S. senator before becoming vice president. She plans to stay engaged in national politics as she considers future roles. Harris added, “I want to travel the country. I want to listen to people. I want to talk with people. And I don’t want it to be transactional where I’m asking for their vote.” Harris added, “In this moment where people have become so deflated and despondent and afraid, those of us who have the ability — which I do right now, not being in an office or in a campaign for that office, to be out there and to talk with folks and remind them of their power.” John Baker covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
